source: GROUND.md §6.6 (G5, raiding). Raid costs are Rust's well-known tables, which the owner allows: how many of each explosive break each grade of wall (timed charge 1/2/4/8 for wood, stone, metal, armoured; rockets 2/4/8/15; bag charges 3/10/23/46; tin grenades 13/46/112/223; explosive rounds 49/185/400/799) and each door (timed charge 1/1/2/2 for wooden, sheet metal, garage and armoured; rockets 1/2/3/4; bag charges 2/4/9/12; explosive rounds 19/63/150/200). The damage of one hit is set so those counts come out on our hit points (RustMVP's 10/200/500/1000/2000; doors 200/250/600/1000), so against wood (200, Rust's 250) and the armoured door (1000, Rust's 800) it differs from Rust's while the counts match. Damage is kept to the fraction, so a grenade's 8.99 against metal takes 112, not 100. Explosives hurt both sides of a wall alike (Rust); a grade may give [hard, soft] to tune that. The tin grenade's doors and the high-velocity rocket are ours, in proportion. Radii, falloff (full within 40% of the radius, nothing at it), the 30% splash on other pieces in sight and shielding by what is in the way are hollow-orbit's (js/game/construct.js explode, js/game/items.js EXPLOSIVE), as are the flesh damage of the charge, rocket and bag; the timed charge's 10 s fuse is RustMVP's and Rust's; the bag charge's 6-12 s fuse and one-in-five dud, and the grenade's, are Rust's in kind. Deployable damage, throws, bounces and the alerts' timing are ours.
